How the Cantor and Evernorth (XRPN) deal actually works:

Evernorth has the option, not the obligation, to sell new shares to Cantor Fitzgerald’s CF Principal Investments over roughly 14 months. Evernorth chooses the timing and size.

When it does, Cantor buys at 97% of that day’s VWAP, and Evernorth keeps the cash. Cantor then resells the shares in the market. Evernorth receives nothing from those resales.

Cantor’s ownership is capped at 4.99%, so this is a financing tool and not a strategic stake.

No shares have been sold yet. The facility only becomes usable after the SEC clears the resale registration.

operator_drafts.draft_en:
U.S. Bank ran its stablecoin pilot on Stellar, a public, open-source network.

Their Jamie Walker put the reason in one line: historically, the most successful networks tend to be public.

He sits down with Denelle Dixon at Meridian (Oct 28-29) to talk about staying compliant while moving onchain.

Banks picking public rails is the story I'm watching this week 🫡
